scope: isolated PostgreSQL notification-outbox recovery and capacity-status exercise

checks: handler execution receives the stable source event id and duplicate handling enqueues once
changed payload under a reused event/channel identity is rejected
disabled provider remains unclaimed without consuming an attempt
crash after fake send is reclaimed; retry reuses the stable idempotency key
transport failure enters retryable state with backoff; a later retry succeeds
operator replay after a full retry budget preserves monotonic attempt history
operator replay and disposal both write audit rows
notification CLI help exposes the new commands
capacity status reports total/open rows, oldest-open age, relation bytes, and deterministic critical threshold state

limitations: Migration 375 was applied only to this fresh scratch database; candidate and legacy databases were not changed.
Receiver-side idempotency is not guaranteed; external delivery remains at-least-once if a receiver ignores Idempotency-Key.
Capacity reporting is advisory and covers the three outbox relations; it does not inspect database-volume free space or send an external alert.
No temporal retention interval or archive mechanism has been approved; no rows are automatically pruned.
Sensor anomaly alert/claim and actuator effects remain outside this outbox implementation.
